YOUR FRAME IS THE BUILD

Nine frames, and none of them is a stat line with a different colour. The Corvette deals a fourth card at every level-up. The Duelist carries its first gun twice — and pays for it with two fewer hardpoints. The Revenant fights better the closer it is to dead. The Prospector gets more out of the same wreckage and simply levels while everyone else is still counting. Each frame rewrites a rule of the run; the numbers are the least interesting thing about it.

GUNS THAT BECOME OTHER GUNS

Ten weapons across five families — autocannon, missile, laser, plasma and railgun. Every one has four tiers, and a tier is not "+10% damage": it is a new firing pattern. Volleys become spreads, spreads become orbits, orbits become spirals that never travel toward anything at all. Push the right pair together and a weapon evolves outright, into chain lightning that hunts through the pack or a burn that keeps killing after you have stopped looking.

THE SHIP YOU CAN SEE LEVELLING

Armour plates, a second engine, then a third, swept antennae, a dorsal rack, a halo in your frame's own colour. Your hull physically grows across a run, and every gun you mount is drawn on the hardpoint it actually fires from. At minute fifteen you can tell what someone built just by looking at their ship.

BOSSES THAT DO NOT STOP COMING

Ten of them, in rotation, and beating one only sets the timer for the next at a higher rank. They arrive with sweeping barrages, homing salvos, tracking beams, blast zones and summoned escorts — and with weapon arms you can shoot off, permanently, if you would rather fight the rest of it unarmed.

RUNS THAT PAY INTO THE NEXT ONE

Eleven unlock conditions turn a bad run into a better next one: frames, weapons and permanent extra hardpoints, tracked per profile. Five difficulties, from a Recruit pass to a Nightmare that is not being polite about it.

Iron Ledger is a high-pressure management sim about building a defense contractor from nothing and keeping it alive under constant financial, operational, and regulatory pressure.

You start with no facilities, no staff, no contracts, and very little room for error. To survive, you’ll need to secure government work, expand your production floor, hire engineers and operators, manage supply chains, maintain compliance, and keep your cash flow ahead of payroll, taxes, and penalties. Every decision affects the health of the company. Miss deadlines, overload your systems, or let your runway collapse, and the market will make the decision for you.

At the center of Iron Ledger is a numbers-driven industrial sandbox built around real pressure points. Materials have to be sourced. Facilities have to be built and staffed. Power has to be generated and balanced across the network. Research opens the door to more advanced production lines, but growth brings heavier scrutiny, steeper costs, and more complex contracts. What starts as a small manufacturing operation can become a sprawling defense enterprise handling aircraft, naval platforms, and strategic programs with enormous reputational and financial stakes.

As your company matures, new opportunities appear beyond the standard contract board. Restricted bio-chemical defense programs add a higher-risk strategic layer, challenging you to fund specialized facilities, absorb major up-front costs, and deliver countermeasures under tight timelines and intense pressure. Treat them as a side project and you will waste money. Build toward them properly and they can become one of the most lucrative and dangerous arms of the business.

Iron Ledger is about expansion under pressure. It is about choosing when to scale, when to conserve cash, when to absorb risk, and when to walk away from work your company is not ready to handle. The goal is not just to grow. The goal is to stay solvent, deliver on time, and survive long enough to become indispensable.

Key Features

  • Build a defense manufacturing company from a bare-bones startup into a major contractor

  • Secure contracts, manage deliveries, and protect your reputation with reliable execution

  • Expand across interconnected production systems, facilities, staffing, utilities, and logistics

  • Balance cash flow against payroll, upkeep, quarterly taxes, penalties, and research spending

  • Unlock advanced product lines through research, from lower-tier equipment to major strategic programs

  • Manage power generation and grid strain as your industrial footprint grows

  • Navigate compliance pressure, export controls, and government scrutiny as you move into higher-tier work

  • Develop a classified bio-defense division to handle high-value biological and chemical threat programs

  • Adapt to cascading bottlenecks in labor, materials, energy, and timing as the company scales

  • Play a single-player management experience focused on planning, optimization, and operational survival

★ Free demo: 6+ hours of gameplay in 4 languages

Lead the Campaign

Humanity's last elite military force wages a desperate war from the decks of the starship Asgard. As enemy armies tighten their grip on the world, you and your companions must reclaim strategic territories, recover vital resources, and push the front lines ever forward.

Fight Beside Your Squad

Take direct control of your character in battle or switch between party members as the fighting unfolds. From desperate defensive actions to full-scale assaults, every mission places you at the center of the war.

Command Your Forces

Train troops, construct military infrastructure, and deploy powerful battlefield assets to secure victory. Sharpshooters, Medics, Tanks, Turrets, and more stand ready to join the fight.

Upgrade the Asgard

Return to your starship between missions to expand facilities, unlock new capabilities, equip your forces, and prepare for the next stage of the campaign.

Experience a Character-Driven Story

Fight alongside Annie and a growing cast of companions as friendships are tested, secrets emerge, and the true scale of the conflict begins to unfold.

Features

  • Story-driven anime-inspired sci-fi campaign

  • Real-time combat with powerful stratagem abilities

  • Switch freely between party members during battle

  • Build, Train, and Command military units

  • Upgrade and expand the starship Asgard

  • Persistent equipment and progression systems

  • Large-scale battles across diverse environments

  • Character interactions, events, and visual novel storytelling

The map is the prize.

Ancient Monoliths stand across Veyra, the Flux Moon. Infuse your troops with Flux to push beyond the limits of your technology, survive the moon, and prepare to expand.

Three civilizations. No way home.

Veyra's ore is the key to crossing the stars. Three civilizations have each sent a small seed force to claim it. None of them can go home, and none can bring more until a Flux relay stands. The moon is not empty: its native life reacts to every mine.

  • Cindral Vanguard, from the industrial world Kharos. The anvil: units that stand still near their own completed structures take less damage.

  • Zephyrine Court, from Aurelion, ruled by scientific houses. The knife: every unit is faster than its rivals, with thinner hulls.

  • Pelagic Choir, from the ocean world Neryth. The chorus: no speed or armour trade-off, dependable everywhere.

All three share the economy, the Monoliths and the core roster. Doctrine is what sets them apart.

Build fast, fight everywhere

Metal and energy stream in every second and are spent as you build. Queue up to 10 orders per factory, loop production, and spread a queue across every factory you select. Siphon Flux, the rare third resource, from shards to field elite units. Fight on land, at sea and in the air with 15 unit classes, and upgrade field structures to MK2 and MK3.

Features

  • Two game modes: Ascendancy and Annihilation, plus optional Horde Attacks, where waves of native creatures hit every base, sooner and bigger each time

  • Skirmish against AI on 32 hand-built maps for 2 to 8 commanders, plus a map generator with nine terrain styles

  • Teams, start positions, 16 player colours, army size and bot difficulty for each seat

  • Online multiplayer through Steam for up to 8 players: host with a 6-digit join code or invite friends

  • If the host crashes, the match can be resumed with everyone back in their seats

  • Basic Training: three missions that teach the controls, the economy and how to take a Monolith. The three faction campaigns are coming soon.

  • Watch All Bots: turn any setup into a spectator battle at 1x to 16x speed

  • Saves and replays, built on a deterministic simulation

  • In-game Getting Started guide covering controls, factions, modes, settings and lore

YOUR BASE IS MOVING, YOUR CREW IS BREAKING. EVERY HIT MATTERS

Irondrive is a top-down vehicular roguelike where crew management meets base building on wheels.

Manage your crew, prioritize tasks, automate repairs, and fix critical systems to survive relentless attacks while your base keeps moving through a hostile wasteland.

Every decision matters, and everything can fall apart fast.

YOUR CREW, YOUR RULES

Every crew member comes with their own traits, skills, and quirks, some thrive under pressure, others crack. Assign jobs, manage hunger and injuries, and keep morale from collapsing as the wasteland wears everyone down.

BUILD YOUR MOVING FORTRESS

Construct and upgrade modules in real time: weapons, storage, crew quarters, repair bays, and more. Every module you add changes how your base fights, survives, and moves, there's no single "right" way to build the Irondrive.

THE ROAD IS NEVER THE SAME TWICE

Travel across a hostile wasteland full of dynamic events and enemy vehicles. Choose your route, scavenge for resources, and brace for whatever the road throws at you. Raiders, ambushes, and threats that force you to adapt on the fly.

NO RUN EVER GOES THE SAME

Permadeath and emergent chaos mean every playthrough tells a different story. Fire breaks out. Systems fail. Crew panics. Survive long enough, and you might just make it to the next horizon.

FEATURES

• Automated and prioritized crew work management system

• Twitch Multiplayer Mode: viewers can spawn their own crew member and issue jobs and orders to help the streamer survive

• Build and repair your moving base in real time

• Manage crew needs: hunger, injuries, panic, and morale

• Defend against enemy vehicles while on the move

• Dynamic damage system: fire, breaches, system failures

• Crew traits that shape how your team plays

• Emergent chaos: no run ever goes the same

Press Kit:

Ironfields is a single-player RTS about capturing the battlefield, not building a base from scratch.

Each mission starts with key structures already placed across the map. You capture them, repair them, defend them, build towers around them, upgrade your units, and decide when it is finally safe to push forward.

The pace is slower and more tactical than a typical click-heavy RTS. You are not meant to win by fast reflexes. You win by holding the right positions, surviving constant pressure, and using the tools each mission gives you.

Capture key buildings
You do not build a traditional base. Instead, you fight for factories, power plants, satellites, and other strategic structures already placed on the battlefield. Every building you secure changes the balance of the mission.

Survive constant enemy pressure
The enemy does not wait for clean scripted waves. It keeps sending units, forcing you to defend, repair, reposition, and slowly turn the map in your favor.

Use airstrikes and towers to break stalemates
Some defenses cannot be pushed through by tanks alone. Build towers, upgrade your units, and call in airstrikes when you need to destroy a key target or open a path forward.

Ironfields focuses on tactical decisions, map control, and hand-crafted single-player missions inspired by older RTS games.

Features

  • Single-player RTS focused on planning and positioning

  • No traditional base building

  • Capture, repair, and defend battlefield structures

  • Build towers and upgrade your units

  • Call in airstrikes to support your attacks

  • Slower-paced tactical gameplay

  • Hand-crafted missions with strong map-control focus

  • Built-in layout editor for custom combat layouts

Make Reversi More Free.

Is This Reversi? is a tabletop sandbox where you can freely handle a Reversi board and its pieces.

Unlike a typical Reversi game, the system does not force legal moves, turns, or the end of the game. How the board and pieces are used is left up to the players.

Freely Control the Board and Pieces

Pieces on the board can be freely placed, moved, flipped, and removed.

You can play Reversi from the beginning, create any board position you like, or start from a position in the middle of a game.

Reversi Without Enforced Rules

“You can’t place a piece there.”
“It’s not your turn.”
“The game ends here.”

Is This Reversi? does not force these decisions on you.

Like playing with a physical board and pieces on a table, players can look at the board, move the pieces, and decide for themselves which rules to follow.

An Electronic Tabletop Playset

Experiment with board positions on your own, play Reversi with another player, or try out your own ways of playing.

Is This Reversi? is not just a Reversi game focused on winning and losing. It is an “electronic tabletop playset” designed to let you freely use the Reversi board and pieces themselves.

The iron remembers every oath. So will you.

You come to the Isenmarch with a vow already heavy across your shoulders. What you do with it is yours to decide — and yours to pay for.

Speak your intent. The Isenmarch answers.

A Machine Game Master narrates your journey and responds to the choices you make — no branching menus, no script to uncover. The Isenmarch answers in cold, spare prose, and the story bends around what you do. It plays to find out what happens. So do you.

Swear vows. Roll the dice. Live with the results.

Isentroth runs a full dice ruleset beneath the story — you see the saga, not the machinery. Forge a character across five ways of being (Fleet, Mettle, Isen, Sleight, Wits). Swear vows and mark their progress toward triumph or ruin. Resolve the hard moments on the dice — your action die against the two dark dice of fate. Ride your momentum high, or watch it break. Bind companions that fight and bleed beside you. Death is matter-of-fact. The world registers it and moves on.

A cold, indifferent frontier.

The Wrackshore gives up its dead slowly. The Frithlands hold their weather like a grudge. Iron is sacred here, oaths bind, and the ruins are just ruins — old and worn and strange. Bog iron. Black water. A raven that calls once and does not call again.

Every saga is its own.

Paths, companions, rituals, and combat talents shape a character no one else will play. The Machine Game Master seeds people, places, and troubles you won't see coming. Begin again and the Isenmarch is the same — and nothing is.

"The world has teeth and does not explain itself."

An internet connection is required to play. Isentroth is rated 18+.

Welcome to Iskarn ! a vast, unforgiving voxel world where every block can be shaped, every hill can be mined, and every night could be your last. Lead a small group of settlers through the wilderness, build a colony from nothing, and defend it against the hordes that rise after dark. How long will your settlement stand?

Build Your Settlement

Raise walls, lay floors, and furnish rooms block by block. From humble shelters to fortified strongholds, every building is yours to design. Your citizens' comfort depends on the quality of their quarters: a warm bed, a lit torch, and solid walls make all the difference.

Gather & Craft

Chop trees, mine deep for ores, harvest crops, and smelt metals across 7 specialized workstations. Forge copper and iron weapons, cook hearty meals, weave cloth into bandages, and arm your people for what comes at night. Over 30 recipes to master.

Explore a Procedural World

Every world is unique. Venture through dense taiga forests, dry steppes, frozen tundra, and green plains, each biome with its own resources and challenges. Dig into mountains, carve tunnels, and reshape the land however you see fit. The world stretches endlessly, there's always something beyond the next hill.

Manage Your People

Each citizen is unique, brave or cowardly, hardworking or lazy. Equip them with forged gear, assign them tasks, and watch them live. They chop, build, craft, eat, sleep, and fight on their own. Keep them warm, fed, and sheltered, or lose them to the cold.

Survive the Night

When darkness falls, the dead rise. Zombie hordes assault your settlement in waves that grow stronger each night. Fortify your walls, arm your citizens, and choose your stance, defend behind barricades or charge into the fray. Every sunrise is earned.

Key Features

  • Infinite procedurally generated voxel world with 4 distinct biomes

  • Full block building, place, dig, rotate, and destroy freely

  • 30+ crafting recipes across 7 workstations

  • Citizens with unique personalities, traits, and autonomous AI

  • Day/night cycle with dynamic weather, seasons, and temperature

  • Zombie horde survival with escalating waves

  • Equipment progression: wood → copper → iron

  • Farming, cooking, and survival mechanics

  • Dig underground, mine ores, carve tunnels, shape the terrain

  • 5 languages: English, French, German, Polish, Russian

After the Otherworld invasion, one island base is all that is left

The Otherworld invasion tore the mainland apart, and the Federation's defense line fell back step by step until only this island base remained.

In the fallen labs, the scientists all made the same choice — upload their complete personality data into the base's central AI, the Core, and leave their bodies in the ruins.

Sion, Iris, Vera, Greta, Erin. They are no longer human, yet they are still part of the line.

Island Core is a single-player monster-horde defense game: you command a Core that keeps upgrading, and a group of the dead who refuse to stop firing.

You are the Core: it handles the firepower, you make the choices

The Core acquires targets, fires and reloads on its own. What you decide is what it becomes —

· Five Core research lines: Alloy Material (Core HP), Intelligence System (experience gain), Armor-Piercing Rounds (damage), Extended Magazine (magazine size) and Agile Mechanism (fire rate)

· Stronger every level: kills grant experience, and each level lets you pick an upgrade from the passive pool; chosen passives keep leveling up

· The Core is your life: if it falls, the run is over. Survive, and you get to upgrade again

Characters: five scientists, five completely different playstyles

Each character brings a full weapon module set, an active skill and a 15-level growth path — they are not skins, they are five builds:

· Sion · Rapid Fire Core — every Core level pushes the fire rate higher; the longer you live, the wilder it gets

· Iris · Laser Weapon — 'Laser Overload': doubled laser damage, doubled range and infinite penetration for a few seconds

· Vera · Saw Gun — blades that carve back and forth with infinite penetration and no penetration falloff; the more they pierce, the harder they hit

· Greta · DCI Machine Gun — a six-barrel minigun that never reloads; 'Firestorm' dumps 200 rounds and double fire rate

· Erin · Drone — spend energy to forge drone turrets, and unlock 'Swarm Control' at level 10 for coordinated strikes

18 weapons, and every one has a temper

These are not reskinned stat sticks:

· Ballistic Storm — fire rate climbs through the magazine and resets on reload

· MK-25 Kinetic SMG — every round missing from the magazine adds damage

· Saw Gun / Phase Sniper Rifle — infinite penetration: blades carve through the horde, rounds phase through space

· Matter Decomposer — restores Core HP equal to the damage it deals

· DV5 Drone — summons sniper-armed drones that pour out lethal armor-piercing rounds

· Prairie Wolf — +25% base crit and +150% crit damage; one shot decides everything

· Standard ballistics: Pistol, SMG, Shotgun, Rapid Cannon, Sniper Rifle, Echo Shotgun

· Sustained damage: Laser Weapon, Flamethrower, Matter Decomposer

· Summons: Drone, DV5 Drone, Electromagnetic Saw System

28 passives — and they combine

Passives are more than stat boosts: some can be crafted into higher-tier modules, fusing basics like Rapid Fire Core and Charge Amplification into brand-new weapon talents.

Some passives are restricted to specific characters or weapons: the same gun is a different gun in different hands.

Three maps, three ways to die

· Desert — a vast desert where periodic sandstorms slow the Core's fire rate and cut its accuracy

· Swamp — irregular downpours: monsters gain +20% movement speed while the Core loses 25% fire rate and 1 attack

· Snowfield — a snowfield fraught with peril

Every map has escalating difficulty tiers, unlocked by completing a run. Monsters unlock as survival time passes and trigger dedicated spawn windows, while timed bosses charge straight at the Core.

Current content

· 5 playable characters, each with a 15-level growth path, exclusive weapon modules and an active skill

· 18 weapon modules + 28 passive upgrades + passive crafting recipes

· 5 Core research lines, plus Core Boost / Super Core Boost

· 3 maps (Snowfield / Desert / Swamp) × multiple difficulty tiers × timed bosses

· Full Simplified Chinese, plus English / 日本語 / 한국어 / Español

Turn a wild island into a thriving, self-running production network.

In Islandry, you oversee the entire island from above. Gather resources from the wild, build farms and processing machines, connect everything with conveyor belts, and let drones handle the work. Your job is to design the system, keep it flowing, and grow your operation across the island.

Build the Island

Everything starts with the island itself.

Catch fish from coastal waters, harvest wild grass, gather plants from the meadows, and bring livestock back to your farms. Some natural resources regrow, while others are limited, encouraging you to spread your operation farther across the island as you expand.

Place the machines you need, connect new production areas, and gradually transform the untouched landscape into an organized network of farms, processing lines, and logistics.

Automate Production

Build production lines using conveyor belts, storage, splitters, filters, junctions, and processing machines.

Draw conveyor lines across the island, route different goods where they need to go, buffer production in storage, and keep every part of the network supplied. Maintain your line and improve the layout when the bottleneck happen.

Meanwhile, drones gather resources, deliver supplies, feed farms, and collect their output automatically.

You build the system. The island keeps it moving.

Sustain the Network

Your farms depend on resources produced somewhere else on the island.

Harvest grass and process it into Plant Feed to keep your crops growing. Use the corn you produce to create Animal Feed, then supply your chicken farms and collect their eggs.

As the network grows, individual production lines begin to depend on one another. A shortage in one part of the island can slow another, while a well-designed supply chain keeps everything running smoothly.

Route and Optimize

A growing island needs more than production.

Split busy conveyor lines, merge resources together, filter specific goods, launch items across gaps and crossing belts, and use storage to keep important supplies available where they are needed.

Upgrade machine and conveyor speeds as demand increases, reorganize inefficient sections, and expand your network as nearby natural resources run low.

From a single production line to an island-wide system, every connection becomes part of a larger operation.

Ship Your Goods

The Export Depot connects your island to trading destinations across the sea.

Choose a trade destination, prepare the goods you want to export, or import resources your production network needs. Ships carry goods between your island and other locations, and each completed transaction returns with money, Island XP, and reputation.

As your Island Rank grows, unlock more trade destinations and expand your options for buying, selling, and moving goods across the sea.

Islandry is designed as a cozy automation experience without combat or survival pressure. Start with the resources found along the shore and meadows. Build the machines. Connect the lines. Keep the island supplied. Then watch a wild island become a production system of your own design.

Story

A nameless monk sits down to meditate beneath a sacred tree in Neo-Osaka, only to discover he has been cursed by the Time Yokai. Helplessly, he tries to rid his body of the corruption — a curse on Time. He must track down and eradicate the Time Yokai so his own soul can be purified. The mechanics of his curse are punishing: as the monk moves, the world around him grinds to a crawl, but the moment he stops, the world tirelessly accelerates, moving faster and faster. Without rest, he must take on bounties to hunt down and vanquish Yokai to save himself. Survive relentless waves and bend reality as you make your way to the final confrontation to strike down the Time Yokai himself.

Wall jumps

Ground slam 

Ground slam jump
